For a family of five, buy a 9 kg, 1400 rpm freestanding washing machine. It is the sensible sweet spot under £400: enough room for everyday loads and bedding without becoming oversized or slow.

## Best pick if you can find it at £400 or less
Samsung Series 5+ WW90CGC04DAEEU — 9 kg, 1400 rpm
Usually around £330–£400.

Why it’s a good buy:
• Proper 9 kg family capacity
• 1400 rpm spin helps reduce drying time
• Typically A-rated for energy
• EcoBubble does well on cooler washes
• Usually comes with a decent Samsung warranty package—check the retailer and register it promptly
• Standard-sized enough for most kitchen/utility spaces

## Strong alternative
LG F4Y509WWLA — 9 kg, 1400 rpm
Often £350–£400.

Choose the LG instead if it is the same price or cheaper. LG machines are generally well regarded, have a quiet direct-drive motor, and usually include useful steam/hygiene programmes. Check the exact warranty terms, as motor warranty and full-machine warranty are not always the same thing.

## If you need a bigger drum for duvets
Look for a Beko 10 kg / 1400 rpm model, such as one in the B5/BM5 range, at roughly £300–£380. Good value, especially if you routinely wash king-size bedding, but I’d pick the Samsung or LG first if prices are close.

## Before ordering
1. Measure the depth, not just the width. Many 9 kg machines are about 55–60 cm deep, plus hoses and door clearance.
2. Check whether the displayed price includes delivery, fitting and old-machine removal—these can add £30–£70.
3. Avoid a cheap washer-dryer at this budget if possible. A separate dryer or drying rack is usually less troublesome and gives more usable capacity.
4. Don’t be swayed by very high spin speeds: 1400 rpm is plenty; reliability and capacity matter more.

Short answer: buy the Samsung WW90CGC04DAEEU if it’s under £400 delivered, or the LG F4Y509WWLA if that is cheaper / available locally.
